summary: This annual survey covers institution-reported enrollment and instructional activity occurring from July 1, 2018, through June 30, 2019. It applies to IPEDS institutions eligible for Title IV participation that have undergraduate enrollment, with reporting aggregated at the institution level across the full 12-month period rather than for a single term. The measures are especially useful for institutions with nontraditional calendars or short-term programs.

The Completions survey covers awards, degree or certificate recipients, and program offerings reported for the July 1, 2018–June 30, 2019 reporting period by postsecondary institutions included in IPEDS. Records are institution-based, with some tables providing one record per institution and others providing multiple records by program or award level. The survey concerns institutions and programs reporting postsecondary completions; its counts are organized by award, recipient, program, and institutional reporting categories rather than individual-level records.

Fall Enrollment covers students enrolled at IPEDS institutions during the fall reporting period. Traditional academic-year institutions report enrollment as of October 15 or their official fall reporting date; institutions with differing or continuous calendars report students enrolled at any time from August 1 through October 31. The unit is the institution, with tables generally containing multiple institution-level records, and the survey applies to institutions in the IPEDS fall-enrollment reporting universe, subject to table-specific eligibility restrictions.

Finance collects annual institutional financial data for the fiscal year ending within the applicable reporting period, with institutions reporting according to their accounting standards. The unit of observation is the institution; the universe is eligible and participating postsecondary institutions, with reporting requirements varying by institution type and degree-granting status. The survey covers institutional revenues, expenditures, assets, liabilities, and related financial resources, but detailed expenditures by function and the natural classifications of fringe benefits, operations and maintenance of plant, depreciation, and interest are unavailable beginning with fiscal year 2016.

The 2019 Graduation Rates component was collected from December 4, 2019, through February 5, 2020, and reports student status as of August 31, 2019. Its unit of observation is the institution’s full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate cohort, with outcomes reported for eligible Title IV institutions that have such undergraduates; cohort definitions and follow-up periods vary by institution sector and program level. The component covers completion and, where applicable, transfer outcomes within specified percentages of normal time.

The Human Resources component covers institutional staff during the fall payroll snapshot, academic-year salary reporting, and the applicable new-hire period, with records organized at the institution level and repeated for occupational or staff-category breakdowns. It applies to postsecondary institutions eligible for IPEDS human-resources reporting; detailed instructional-staff and new-hire tables further restrict coverage to degree-granting institutions with at least 15 full-time employees and related administrative offices. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was mandatory in odd-numbered years and optional in even-numbered years beginning in 2001, and became mandatory annually beginning in 2016.

Institutional Characteristics data were collected during the fall 2019 window, September 4–October 16, 2019, for the 2019-20 academic year. The universe is every institution in the 2019-20 IPEDS universe, with Title IV-participating institutions required to report; records are primarily institution-level, though some tables contain program or comparison-group-member records. Some characteristics are supplemented or updated from winter and spring IPEDS collections.

This survey covers student financial aid received during July 1, 2018–June 30, 2019 and reports institution-level data for postsecondary institutions eligible for IPEDS reporting, with student populations defined separately by table. Reporting concerns undergraduate and, for military and veterans benefits, graduate students; the data are organized by aid type, source, and recipient population rather than by individual student. Most Student Financial Aid reporting is annual, while military servicemember and veterans-benefits reporting follows an odd/even-year availability rule described with that table.
